summary: Free AI assistant with WhatsApp access
html:
Free.
Works through WhatsApp.
You can literally send it a voice note like you would to an employee, and it starts working on the task.

It’s called Instinct, and I’ve been playing with it for the last few days.

There’s almost nothing new to learn.

You text it, send a voice note, or talk to it and tell it what you want done.

It can research, browse websites, use accounts you connect, contact people and businesses, make bookings and purchases, follow up, and keep working on a task over time.

It can even have its own email address, so you can send it to communicate with a business or supplier and let it handle the conversation itself.

And one of the newest features really feels like a glimpse into the future:
Your Instinct can now talk directly to someone else’s Instinct.

I can send my AI assistant to coordinate a meeting with your AI assistant, and let them figure it out between them.

The traction around it is pretty crazy too.

It already has more than 100,000 users, and this week it was reported that the company is in talks to raise $1 billion at around a $10 billion valuation. Just a few weeks ago it was valued at $2.5 billion.

Of course, there is a tradeoff: access and privacy.

An assistant that can do this much for you also needs access to a lot of your digital life. Instinct has already received criticism around privacy, security, and how much autonomy an agent like this should have.

So I’m definitely interested, but for now I’m being selective about what I connect to it.

Instinct is currently free and access is still limited while they scale.

I have 25 invites for the group.

If you want to try it, DM me by tomorrow and I’ll send you one. If more than 25 people want in, I’ll try to get more.

Jay

summary: Seedance 2.5 improves Amazon product videos
html:
Seedance 2.5 Changes How We Create Product Videos

ByteDance released Seedance 2.5 recently, and it’s the most important AI video models for product content.

The biggest change isn’t just better-looking video.

It’s the workflow.

Here are the updates I think matter most for Amazon sellers:

1. You can use video as a reference

This might be my favorite update.

Until now, we mostly gave AI images of our product and tried to explain how it should move.

Now we can simply show it.

A mechanism opening. A product folding. Liquid pouring. Fabric moving. A kitchen tool being used.

If your product has movement or functionality that’s difficult to communicate with a still image, this is a huge improvement.

You can provide up to 50 references in one generation: 30 images, 10 videos, and 10 audio clips.

2. Up to 30 seconds in one generation

Until now, creating a 30-second AI product video usually meant generating several short clips and stitching them together afterward.

Now you can describe the entire sequence and generate it together, with much better continuity between shots.

And I think 30 seconds is already a great length for an Amazon product video. Long enough to show the product, demonstrate it, add some emotion, and finish with a strong hero shot.

3. Prompt understanding has improved a lot

You can be much more specific about what should happen in each part of the video, camera movement, timing, product actions, shot changes, and more.

My advice: give it more detail, not less.

The more clearly you describe what you want, the better it seems to follow the plan.

4. You can edit specific moments

Something went wrong around second 12?

Seedance 2.5 supports timestamp-based editing, so you can target that section instead of automatically starting the entire video again.

What I still don’t love

The main thing I still don’t love is the music, text, and voiceover it generates itself.

I prefer generating the video first and adding those afterward.

Or, more accurately, letting Claude add them for me with one click 😄

🎬 The real shift

Until now, AI video models were great at making clips.

Seedance 2.5 is starting to feel like something you can actually ask to direct an entire product video.

📌 On Wednesday, August 19 at 2 PM ET, we’re going live again to show exactly how we’re using Seedance 2.5 to create product videos.

From the references and prompting all the way to the final video.

Spots are limited, and there will be no recording.

https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/K1oTVcBsToiUao_nNdRtCw

Jay

summary: Use Fable 5 for serious work only
html:
2 days left on Fable 5. Do not waste them on nonsense.

Yesterday I burned through my entire Fable 5 limit, the new, monstrous model in Claude Code, on my main account's plan. So I opened a second paid account just to keep using it for two more days.

And it honestly hurts to watch what people waste it on.

You have access to a model that a year ago felt like science fiction. It does phenomenal work, it barely asks you questions, and it runs for hours on its own. And a lot of people are just playing with it.

So listen up.

spend the two days you have left on the heavy work, on building your infrastructure:

🔸 Plan how your whole AI setup should actually work, from the ground up.
🔸 Build your agents and automations right, for the long run.
🔸 Let it go through your old skills and improve them.
🔸 The complex problem that needs hours of real thinking.

Everything else, send to the small models.

You have until July 7, under the plan you already pay for. After that every use of it costs extra (and it will not be cheap).

💡 And it burns your limit fast, so run it in Plan Mode: it shows you the full plan first and you approve before it runs. Saves a lot.

Hit 👍 if you want more practical tips like this.

Jay
